newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan sends food to starving Red Sea state.
newsitem.headline: Sudan sends food to starving Red Sea state.

text.p: The Sudanese government has distributed sorghum in the northeastern Red Sea state that last week appealed for help to end a famine threatening 240,000 people, an official newspaper said on Saturday.
The army's bi-weekly al-Nasr paper said the sorghum, Sudan's staple food, was given to displaced people in several towns in Red Sea state.
The paper quoted Abdel-Rahman Balal, commissioner of Tokar province, as saying that that there were 293 displaced families in Tokar alone.

The privately-owned Alwan daily newspaper said last week that according to a report by the state's emergency committee, there was widespread malnutrition among children, women and the elderly in five provinces in Red Sea state.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Cresent Societies (IFRC) in Nairobi has said it was preparing an appeal to assist 158,000 of the 240,000 Beja people in the Red Sea Hills through rations of oil, pulses and cereals.
Two years of crop failure and little rainfall have hit the region hard. The IFRC said that the Beja relied on livestock for survival but grain costs shot up while animal prices fell.
In another development, a parliamentarian from Darfur state has charged the local authorities there with neglecting food shortages in the states, which are west of the capital Khartoum.

The privately-owned al-Rai al-Aam newspaper on Saturday quoted Khalil Adam Abdel-Karim as saying that food shortages in the Darfur states, particularly Northern Darfur, were "threatening the citizens and their health".
The authorities in Darfur have often dismissed reports of food shortages as exaggerated.
